note: Passage 3710 (Pro 1:18-19) — the irony of greed: the ambushers 'lie in wait for their own blood', set an ambush 'for their own lives' (nephesh); unjust gain 'takes away the life (nephesh) of its possessors'. nephesh read as the self/life forfeited (upgraded from seed-qualifier: the self IS the char here, the thing greed consumes). Two distinct occurrences kept apart.

dims.v: their own lives/selves — the very self the ambush recoils upon
the self against which the plotters, unknowing, set their own ambush
paired with 'their own blood' — the self and its life-blood are what they truly hunt

nephesh here is the self/life turned into its own victim — the moral irony: violence plotted outward closes on the plotter's own soul. Read as characteristic (the self at stake), not a mere qualifier.
the life/self that unjust gain seizes from the one who holds it
the life that greed (betsa) 'takes away' from its own possessor
welded to unjust gain (betsa) as the thing that consumes the self
distinct from 264699: here nephesh is the life GREED devours — the general maxim (1:19) that unjust gain costs the greedy their own life. The self is the price of covetousness.
